sections.subtitle: Match context
sections.text: Craven Cottage hosts a close match-up between Fulham (11th, 48 points) and Bournemouth (6th, 52 points). The model views this as near level with a slight away edge and a strong chance that both teams score.

sections.subtitle: Current form
sections.text: Fulham’s last 5: W2-D1-L2, with clean sheets against Brentford and Aston Villa but clear losses to Liverpool and Arsenal. Bournemouth are unbeaten in 5 (W3-D2) and on a 14-match away unbeaten run, producing strong expected goals in wins at Newcastle and Arsenal.

sections.subtitle: Head-to-head
sections.text: Bournemouth won the last 2 meetings (3-1, 1-0) and are unbeaten in the last 3 against Fulham. Recent clashes are often open: over 2.5 goals in 6 of the last 7, and both teams scored in 7 of the last 9. Fulham have not kept a clean sheet in the last 9 meetings.

sections.subtitle: Season stats
sections.text: Fulham: 44 scored, 49 conceded; 57 big chances created (rank 18) and 95 big chances allowed (rank 18). Bournemouth: 55 scored, 52 conceded, and a strong late-goal profile (27% from minutes 76–90). Both sides pose late threats, which can swing close games.

sections.subtitle: Tactics and match-ups
sections.text: Fulham lean on wide service and Harry Wilson’s end product (10 goals, 6 assists), while Raúl Jiménez trails his expected goals. For Bournemouth, Eli Junior Kroupi is in form, Alex Scott drives midfield, and Marcos Senesi’s distribution can target space behind Fulham’s full-backs (he has been a standout in recent meetings). Transitions and late-game phases look decisive.

sections.subtitle: Referee, cards and corners
sections.text: Referee Andy Madley averages 3.1 yellows and 0.11 reds per game. Recent trends point to a moderate card count. Corners profile is medium to slightly high (Fulham 4.7 per game; Bournemouth recently produced high corner volumes), so expect around average-to-above-average totals; projection is about 4 yellows and around 10 corners.

sections.subtitle: Match prediction
sections.text: Close contest with a slight away lean. Bournemouth to edge it, with both teams likely to score.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Match context and first-half flow
halftimeSections.text: Goalless at the break at Craven Cottage, with both Fulham and Bournemouth reduced to 10 players after first-half dismissals. Bournemouth began with the sharper tempo and enjoyed the first meaningful attacking spell, but Fulham grew into control from around the half-hour mark and sustained pressure up to half-time. That late home dominance included a big chance for Rodrigo Muniz and a strike against the woodwork. The match has been open in transition, yet Fulham have looked more cohesive in the final third despite the numerical balance.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Key statistics
halftimeSections.text: Fulham lead possession 59% to 41% and edge expected goals 0.56 to 0.09. Shots on target are 1-0 to the hosts and big chances 1-0. Corners are 4-2 to Fulham. Bournemouth have more final-third entries (38 vs 26), but Fulham have converted territory into more penalty-area entries (18 vs 10). Fulham also lead the physical duels, winning 60% overall and 58% in the air.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Tactical notes
halftimeSections.text: With space opening in a 10 vs 10 scenario, Fulham’s full-backs Timothy Castagne and Antonee Robinson have provided width, while Harry Wilson and Tom Cairney have supplied line-breaking passes. Rodrigo Muniz has occupied the centre-backs well and remains the prime target for crosses and cut-backs. Bournemouth have advanced into the final third frequently but have struggled to access central zones, relying on wide progression without penalty-area penetration. Marcos Senesi and James Hill have defended their box assertively, but Bournemouth need quicker service into Evanilson and more aggressive runs from Marcus Tavernier and Rayan to threaten behind.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Players to watch
halftimeSections.text: Rodrigo Muniz has already had the clearest chance and is positioned to benefit from continued service into the area. Timothy Castagne’s delivery and Wilson’s set-piece and crossing quality are driving Fulham’s chance creation. For Bournemouth, Marcos Senesi has been strong defensively and Adrien Truffert has offered forward thrust; Evanilson’s movement will be key if the visitors commit earlier passes into the box.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Discipline and corners
halftimeSections.text: Each side have 1 red card, and Fulham’s edge in duels suggests continued physical contests. Corners stand at 4-2 to Fulham. Expect a few more cautions in an open second half and a modest rise in corners, with Fulham likely to maintain a slight advantage on set-piece volume.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Second-half outlook
halftimeSections.text: With space across midfield and Fulham carrying the stronger attacking threat before the interval, the hosts look more likely to break the deadlock. Bournemouth’s transitions remain a danger, but their first-half end-product was limited. The balance of play points to Fulham converting one of their box entries after the break, with a narrow home win the most probable outcome.
